text:
**Yes, but only some models can.** A basic power station can keep a computer running in an outage, but without automatic switchover it may cut power for a moment when the grid drops, and that can reboot the PC.

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS or EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a power station works as a UPS only if it has this, plus a suitable transfer time and enough output and battery capacity ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Transfer time.** Look for about 10 ms or less. Anker notes that 10-20 ms is fast but not 0 ms, so check your PC or power supply manual. If it requires 0 ms, you need an online double-conversion UPS ([Anker NAS/server guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). EcoFlow is more cautious and says many "UPS" power stations switch in 20-30 ms or more ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Both are vendors selling their own products, so treat the damage claims with some skepticism and test with your own setup.
- **Pure sine wave output** for computers and monitors.
- **Enough wattage.** Add up your PC, monitor and router draw, ideally measured with a plug-in watt meter, and compare it to the continuous output rating.
- **Pass-through use.** Confirm the manual supports staying plugged in while powering devices, and keep the unit ventilated.

Runtime is roughly battery Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load gives about 8.5 hours at best, and less in practice.

**Options from the results**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave output, 10 ms UPS switchover. The page lists $699.99 after coupon, so confirm the price at checkout.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): 600 W output and under 10 ms switchover, which EcoFlow positions as a smaller, more affordable UPS-style option. That page is a blog post, so check current pricing on EcoFlow's store.
- [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2): 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W, UPS switchover of 15 ms or less. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the listing says was tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24. This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Its slower switchover makes it a weaker fit for a desktop than the first two.

If you only need a few minutes to save work and shut down, a regular desktop UPS is simpler. A power station makes more sense when you want hours of runtime. If you tell me your PC's wattage, or whether it's a laptop or desktop, I can narrow this down.
